draft.title: What changes in an enlargement
card: stay the same. A 50° angle in the original is still 50° in the image.

is multiplied by k². If k = 3, the area is multiplied by 3² = 9.
Example: a square has side 2 cm and area 4 cm². With k = 3, the side is 6 cm and the area is 36 cm², which is 4 × 9.
draft.remember: Angles stay put, lengths go × k, area goes × k².

a.q: A rectangle has area 10 cm². It is enlarged with scale factor 2. What is the area of the image?
a.why: Area is multiplied by k² = 2² = 4, so 10 × 4 = 40 cm². Multiplying by 2 gives 20 cm², which is the mistake of treating area like length.
a.clue: Area is multiplied by k squared.

b.q: A triangle has angles 30°, 60° and 90° and a longest side of 8 cm. It is enlarged with k = 1.5. What are the angle sizes and longest side of the image?
b.why: Angles do not change in an enlargement, so they stay 30°, 60° and 90°. The side is 8 × 1.5 = 12 cm. Multiplying the angles by 1.5 is tempting but wrong, and 9.5 cm comes from adding.
b.clue: One of these quantities does not change at all.
